text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bomb experts comb eastern Nigerian city of Onitsha where four people were killed on Friday in two bomb blasts.
- Nigeria plans to begin exporting telecommunication accessories from next year. They will be produced by a consortium of Turkish and Nigerian companies, officials says.
- The Petroleum Trust Fund, which disburses money accruing from a 1994 pump price increase, has earmarked 2.5 billion naira to rehabilitate 3,860 secondary schools across the country.
- Two new drugs for the treatment of the acquired immune deficiency syndrome virus are now available in Nigeria.
- British Airways will lose an estimated revenue of 17.8 billion naira if the federal government ban on its flights to Nigeria lasts for 12 months.
- Death toll in the eastern Nigerian bomb blasts rise to five following the death on Saturday of a victim who had been in critical condition in hospital.
- Nothern state of Sokoto suspends publication of its The Path newspaper and closes its Rima Radio station because of lack of funds.
- Federal government releases two billion naira to enable contractors complete the construction of National Assembly complex in Abuja in readiness for democratic rule next year.
- Three drug suspects detained in the northern Kebbi state were shot and wounded while trying to escape from jail.
